title: Regret bound for Hedge against an adaptive adversary
statement:
Fix $N \ge 1$ experts, a horizon of $T$ rounds, and a learning rate $\eta > 0$. Consider a full interaction in which the learner runs the Hedge algorithm with learning rate $\eta$ — playing at each round $t$ the exponential-weights distribution $p_t(i) \propto \exp(-\eta L_t(i))$ over the experts, where $L_t(i)$ is the cumulative loss of expert $i$ over rounds $0,\dots,t-1$ — against an adaptive adversary who, having observed the past loss vectors and the learner's current distribution, returns a loss vector with every coordinate in $[0,1]$; let $\ell$ be the loss sequence so generated. Writing $\widehat{L}_T = \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\sum_{i} p_t(i)\,\ell_t(i)$ for the learner's expected cumulative loss and $L^\ast = \min_{i} L_T(i)$ for the loss of the best expert in hindsight, the regret satisfies
\[
  \widehat{L}_T - L^\ast \;\le\; \frac{\log N}{\eta} + \frac{\eta\, T}{8}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: learner plays the Hedge exponential-weights distribution with rate η
adversary is adaptive with loss coordinates in [0,1]
loss sequence is the one generated by the learner–adversary interaction
